newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-BYRNE TO TAKE OVER AS FERRARI DESIGNER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BYRNE TO TAKE OVER AS FERRARI DESIGNER.

text.p: Former Benetton designer Rory Byrne will take over from John Barnard as chief designer at Ferrari next week, the Italian team announced on Tuesday.

Byrne, a South African who had served Benetton for more than a decade, left the team late last year and was thought to have taken early retirement in order to pursue an interest in setting up a diving project in Thailand.

He and Ferrari's recently-appointed new technical director Ross Brawn were seen as the creative force at Benetton in recent years. Brawn also left Benetton in December and joined Ferrari early in the new year.
In a news release, Ferrari confirmed the changes which end the highly-respected Barnard's long association with the team through two spells, one in the 1980s and one in the 1990s.

Barnard had operated as Ferrari's designer from a technical facility he created at Guildford in England, but the team recently took a decision to concentrate all of its activities at its Maranello headquarters in Italy.
The statement said: "Ferrari has reached an agreement in principle aiming at assigning to John Barnard its Ferrari Design and Development facilities at Guildford.

"The facilities will continue to operate totally autonomously in respect of Ferrari, in the field of specialist design and manufacture. Subject to final agreement, it is the parties' intention to implement this project within the next two months.
"Thereafter Ferrari will use the Guildford facilities as one of its suppliers only in the production field."
It added that Byrne would take over as chief designer from February 17.

Barnard, who was very successful as designer of the McLaren cars which won consistently in the late 1980s, is understood to be interested in working with Frenchman Alain Prost, who is keen to create a new all-French team by buying Ligier.
